what_its_for: Lanadelumab-flyo is used to help prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults and children 12 years of age and older. HAE causes sudden episodes of swelling in the face, throat, stomach, hands, feet, or genitals. This medicine does not treat an HAE attack that has already started — it is used to prevent future attacks from happening.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in the stomach area, thigh, or upper arm. A healthcare provider will teach you or a caregiver how to give the injection at home. Always follow your healthcare provider's instructions carefully. Rotate the injection site each time to avoid soreness. Do not inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or hard. Allow the medicine to come to room temperature for about 15 minutes before injecting. Do not shake the vial or prefilled syringe.
dosing: The usual dose is 300 mg given once every 2 weeks by injection under the skin. If your HAE attacks are well controlled, your doctor may reduce the dose to 300 mg every 4 weeks. Always take the dose exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not change your dose or dosing schedule without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give the injection as soon as you remember. Then restart your regular dosing schedule from that date. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store lanadelumab-flyo in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze this medicine and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 6 months — but once removed from the refrigerator, do not put it back. Write down the date you removed it from the refrigerator and throw it away after 6 months if not used. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use if the solution looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles floating in it.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods or drinks known to interact with this medicine. However, let your doctor know about all medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting lanadelumab-flyo. Avoid injecting into skin that is irritated, scarred, or tattooed. Do not share your medicine, needles, or syringes with anyone else.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, dizziness, or trouble breathing; signs of injection site infection such as increasing redness, warmth, pain, or drainage at the injection site; an HAE attack, since this medicine does not treat an attack that is already happening and you will need separate rescue medication; any unusual or bothersome side effects. Common side effects include redness, pain, or bruising at the injection site and dizziness — these are usually mild, but call your doctor if they bother you or do not go away.
when_it_works: Lanadelumab-flyo starts working to prevent HAE attacks within a few weeks of starting treatment. Most patients begin to see a reduction in attack frequency within the first month. It may take up to 70 days to reach full effect in your body. It is important to keep taking this medicine on schedule even if you feel well, since it works best when used consistently as a preventive treatment.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known how this medicine affects an unborn baby or breast milk. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Children: This medicine is approved for use in patients 12 years of age and older. It has not been studied in children younger than 12. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is required for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Dose adjustments are generally not needed for mild to moderate kidney or liver problems, but always inform your doctor about any health conditions you have.
